lines.text: Northwind Bank - Loan Origination Portal
Sprint 14 Review
Date: 12 March 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Delivery Manager), Marcus Webb (Tech Lead), Anita Rao (QA Lead), Tom Fielding (Business Analyst), Jonas Kern (Northwind, Product Owner)

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Morning everyone. Sprint 14 review, we have about forty minutes. Agenda is the same as usual - sprint goal, demo, defects, then UAT readiness and anything for the risk log.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Marcus, do you want to start with where we landed against the sprint goal?

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: Sure. The goal was to complete the document upload service and get the credit decision engine talking to the new rules API. Both are done and merged.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: Document upload went in on Tuesday. We are handling PDF, JPEG and PNG, with the twenty megabyte cap Jonas asked for.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: The rules API integration took longer than we sized it. We estimated five points and it was closer to eight, mostly because their error responses are not consistent.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: Right. We have a wrapper handling both now, so it is contained.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Did that overrun cost us anything else in the sprint?

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: We dropped the audit log export story. It was the lowest priority item and nobody is blocked by it.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Agreed, that carries to Sprint 15.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Anita, defects?

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: We closed eleven and opened four. Three of the four are cosmetic - spacing on the applicant summary screen, a truncated label in Welsh, and a date format that shows US order on one report.

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: The fourth one is more interesting. If an applicant uploads a document and then hits back before the upload finishes, the record ends up with a document reference pointing at nothing.

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: How often would that happen in practice?

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: Rarely, but a branch user on a slow connection could hit it. The record looks complete and is not.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: I'll take that one. It needs the upload to be transactional rather than fire and forget. I should have it done by Thursday.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Marcus to fix the orphaned document reference defect by Thursday. Noted.

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: I'd call that one high severity even though it is low frequency, because the data ends up wrong and nobody knows.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Fair. Let us log it as high.

lines.speaker: Tom Fielding
lines.text: On the demo - I walked Jonas through the applicant journey on Monday and the feedback was good.

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: It was. The one thing I raised was the wording on the affordability declaration. Legal want specific phrasing.

lines.speaker: Tom Fielding
lines.text: Jonas is sending me the approved wording. Once I have it, it is a ten minute change.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Jonas, when do you think you will have that?

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: I'll chase legal this week. I would say by the twentieth.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Tom to update the affordability declaration wording once Northwind legal provides it, expected 20 March.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Now, UAT readiness. This is the part I want to spend time on.

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: We are ready from a build point of view. What we do not have is test data.

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: We need around two hundred anonymised applicant records to exercise the decision engine properly. Synthetic data does not hit the edge cases.

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: That has to come from our side. I will need to talk to the data governance team.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: How long does that normally take at Northwind?

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: Honestly, it varies. Two weeks if it is straightforward, longer if they want a new data sharing agreement.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: UAT starts on the sixth of April. If the data arrives late, we lose the first week of UAT.

lines.speaker: Anita Rao
lines.text: We have been assuming the anonymised data would be available by the end of March. That assumption is not confirmed anywhere.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Then let us put it in the log properly as an assumption, not a fact.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: And the dependency is on Northwind's data governance team providing the anonymised records.

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: Understood. I will raise it on Monday and come back to you with a date.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Jonas to confirm the anonymised test data date with Northwind data governance, by Monday 16 March.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: One more thing. The UAT environment is still pointing at the old rules API endpoint.

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: It needs repointing before UAT or nothing will work. It is a config change, maybe an hour.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Who owns that?

lines.speaker: Marcus Webb
lines.text: Infrastructure, but I can raise the ticket.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Marcus to raise the infrastructure ticket to repoint the UAT environment to the new rules API, before 6 April.

lines.speaker: Tom Fielding
lines.text: Should we flag anything to the steering committee?

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: The test data dependency, yes. Everything else is inside our control.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Overall I would call the project amber rather than green, purely because of the test data. Delivery itself is on track.

lines.speaker: Jonas Kern
lines.text: That seems fair to me. I would rather see amber with a reason than green with a surprise later.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Agreed. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Thanks everyone. Sprint 15 planning is Thursday at ten.

## Overall status: Amber
Project status amber due to test data risk.

## Summary
Sprint 14 achieved its goal of integrating the document upload service and rules API. Defects and UAT readiness issues were identified.

## Progress this period
- Document upload service and rules API integration completed.
- Defect identified: orphaned document reference when navigating back during upload.
- Affordability declaration wording pending legal approval.
- UAT environment still pointing to the old rules API endpoint.

## Next steps
- Resolve orphaned document reference defect.
- Update affordability declaration wording once legal approval is received.
- Confirm anonymised test data availability with data governance.
- Repoint UAT environment to the new rules API.

## Risks and issues
- UAT environment still pointing at the old rules API endpoint.
- Project status amber due to test data risk.

## Support needed from the client
- Provide approved affordability declaration wording.
- Confirm anonymised test data availability and provide records.
- Assist in repointing the UAT environment to the new rules API.
